segments.text: Welcome back to the show. Today we're looking at how speech recognizers handle more than one voice at a time, and why that is harder than it sounds.
Right, because a single speaker is predictable, but a conversation overlaps, interrupts, and changes pace without warning.
Exactly, so keep an ear on the speaker labels as we go. If the engine cannot tell us apart, that is a diarization failure, not a transcription failure.
